title: HVAC sizing follow-up (aux heat, shared walls, sizing for heating, "runs all the time," etc)
summary: A follow-up on heat pump sizing that covers auxiliary heat, dual fuel, gas fixed charges, variable-capacity sizing, shared walls and continuous running.

verdicts.note: Multi-stage and inverter units run at reduced capacity for cooling, limiting the short cycling and humidity problems of heating-based sizing.

Authors state sizing one ton larger for heating is not a concern because variable capacity lets the heat pump match the smaller cooling load by running at lower output; cooling cycling was not measured.

assertions.quote: modern inverter driven equipment of the fancier variety strives to never stop it will just slow down the compressor to match loading

verdicts.note: Fewer starts reduce compressor wear and cycling losses; inverter units modulate to match load.
Ducted ccASHPs generally ran at low capacity for long periods and rarely fired at maximum; compressor wear was not studied.

Despite variable-capacity compressors, the heat pumps were off for a significant fraction of the time at temperatures where continuous running was expected (thermostat schedules or controls); compressor wear was not studied.

Variable-speed modulation allows longer cycles than single-speed on/off cycling, and median heating cycles at 5-30 F ran 50-200 minutes, but some sites mostly cycled under 10 minutes; compressor wear was not studied.

assertions.quote: a furnace which runs for twice as long because it's half the capacity is using the exact same amount of energy

verdicts.note: Fuel use is set by heat delivered and AFUE, not runtime; cycling losses make oversized units only slightly worse.

assertions.quote: my gas furnace doesn't work when the power is out

verdicts.note: Modern furnaces need electricity for ignition, inducer and blower, so they stop in an outage without backup power.
